newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 14.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
PRIME MINISTER OFFERS TO RESIGN AS COALITION CHIEF

Hemmed in by the constituents of the United Front, prime minister Deve Gowda offered to step down as the leader of the Front's parliamentary group to pave the way for a contemplated new arrangement with the Congress party. The United Front agreed in principle to change the leadership of the combine if the Congress so desired. But the action would be contingent upon the resolution of the Congress Working Committee and the quality of support it offered to the Front. Gowda promised full cooperation to the party in whatever step it might take to meet the present situation, United Front sources said.
The Observer
AMENDMENTS TO FINANCE BILL LIKELY

The budget may still remain just a dream, given the Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) opposition to passing the Finance Bill that gives effect to taxation proposals. The Congress and the BJP both indicated they would bring in amendments when the Bill comes up for discussion during the three-day special session starting on April 21. Given their opposition, it was now becoming clear the Bill was unlikely to be passed in its present form, though all the parties agreed for the passage of the same following an appeal from the speaker of the lower house.
The Economic Times
LEFT PARTY PUTS HURDLE IN BUDGET PASSAGE

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPM) came down heavily on the attempt to pass the Finance Bill for 1997/98 (April-March) by describing it as an immoral act. It held the government could at the most take another vote on account for meeting any contingency, but not pass the entire budget. The party's tough line sharply reduced the chances of passing the Finance Bill. The CPM also decided to canvass among other constituents of the Left Front for support to its stand.
FAST-TRACK POWER PROJECT FACES HURDLE

A new counter-guarantee condition was slapped on fast-track power projects. The concerned independent power producers were told that only a portion of their total tax on income would be reimbursed by the respective state electricity boards signing the power purchase agreements. The private investors, who had all taken on significant sums of overseas debt, are virtually up in arms, as the new clause was bound to slash the total cover amount. The projects would no longer be bankable. There were clear indications that the counter-guarantees on the remaining five fast track projects would be delayed.
BRITISH GAS IN FRAY FOR TAKING OVER GUJARAT GAS

British Gas joined Enron Corp and Pacific Enterprise of the United States in their attempt to take over the Gujarat Gas Company. There were also reports that the Gujarat government, which hold a 26 percent stake in the company, and Bharat Petroleum Corporation showing an interest in acquiring a 35 percent stake in the company. British Gas, along with Enron, had emerged as the strongest bidder for the company which has gas marketing rights in Ankleshwar, Surat and Bharuch areas.
FUND NORMS FOR NON BANKING FINANCE FIRMS LOWERED

The minimum net-owned fund stipulation to set up a non-banking finance company had been lowered from five million rupees to 2.5 million. The Reserve Bank of India has, however, decided not to change another clause in the RBI (Amendment) Act of 1997 which gave the central bank more responsibility than it could handle. The Act came into effect from April 1, 1997. The other major change pertained to the RBI's decision to review its stand on the acceptance of deposits from relatives or individuals for business purposes.
Financial Express
PROPOSED FOREIGN EXCHANGE LAW MAY GO SOFT ON OFFENDERS

The compounding of exchange violations and settlement of offences by payment of penalty were among the key recommendations of the draft report on the proposed Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA). The report was believed to be extremely soft on offenders. If accepted, several Foreign Exchange Regulation Act accused might escape penal action by paying penalties. The legislation might be with retrospective effect. A major recommendation of the proposed FEMA was that there would be no provisions relating to adjudication. The draft did not clearly spell out the procedure for compounding of offences.
GOOD SHOW BY INDUSIND; HDFC OUTPACES GLOBAL TRUST

Induslnd Bank consolidated its top position among the new private banks by posting the highest net profit in 1996/97 (April-March). HDFC Bank was likely to pip Global Trust Bank to the second position by recording a 100 percent growth in its net. Unaudited financial results showed Induslnd was set to post a net profit of 650 million rupees for 1996/97, up from 456 million rupees in the previous year. HDFC Bank, which posted a net profit of 210 million rupees in 1995/96, was likely to record a 10 percent jump in net profit. Industry sources said the bank's net profit was expected to be around 420 million rupees in 1996/97.
POLICY DELAY COSTS EXPORTERS OVER FIVE MLN RUPEES

The political turmoil and laxity on the part of the government in taking follow-up measures after the announcement of the new export-import policy has taken a toll on exports. Exporters have lost around five billion rupees in the last 10 days as the government failed to implement the measures announced in the policy. Exporters were still unsure of the amendments and modifications in the policy announced by the commerce minister on March 31, 1997.
HIMACHAL FUTURISTIC SETS UP PROJECT FOR CELLULAR HANDSETS

Himachal Futuristic Commications (HFCL) became the first Indian company to manufacture cellular handsets with the launch of a pilot project at an existing unit. This would make HFCL the first Indian telecommunication company to be manufacturing cellular handsets as well as exporting it. HFCL has procured the technical support of a leading US-based reasearch and development house, company sources said. The compnay has not offloaded any equity in this venture. The US company would be paid royalty as per the agreement reached between the two parties sometime in the previous year, sources said.
Business Standard
UNIT TRUST TO LAUNCH MONEY MARKET MUTUAL FUND

The Unit Trust of India (UTI) would launch its first money market mutual fund on April 23. The fund would be an open-ended scheme with UTI Bank providing sale and repurchase of units. The target corpus of the scheme would be 10 million rupees. UTI aims to mop up the target amount in 30 days and if that failed it would refund the whole amount. Cheques would be credited to the account of investors within 24 hours. The minimum investment would be 10,000 rupees without any upper limit. The sale price would be at par value of 10 rupees when the scheme opens for subscription. Thereafter, sale and repurchase prices would be at net asset value.
TISCO-RYERSON VENTURE CLEARED

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) cleared a Tata Steel proposal for a joint venture with US-based Ryerson. Tatas Ryerson, in which both Tata Iron & Steel Company and Ryerson hold 50 percent equity each, proposes to set up a processing facility to produce customised steel products for the domestic automobile and consumer durables industries. Part of the foreign equity was being brought in by Singapore-based Inland of India with whom Ryerson has a technical collaboration agreement. The FIPB also cleared the proposal of P&O Australia to set up a 6.92 billion rupee container handling facility at Jawaharlal Nehru Port near Bombay.
DUMPING DUTY ON ACRYLIC STAPLE FIBRE IMPORTS

The government decided to impose anti-dumping duty on acrylic staple fibre being imported from the United States, Thailand and South Korea. A notification issued by the Commerce Ministry said barring 1.7 denier acrylic fibre being exported by Cytec Industries Inc of the United States, all other acrylic fibres being exported by the United States, Thailand and Korea to India were below their normal value, resulting in dumping and consequently causing material injury to the Indian industry.
INSTITUTIONS URGED TO REVIEW SUSPENSION OF GUARANTEES

Several mid-cap companies asked the financial institutions (FIs) and the Finance Ministry to reverse recent refusal to extend guarantees for External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) by the companies. The decision would force an estimated 1,500 mid-cap companies to either look to banks to guarantee their overseas loans or be starved of working capital. The FIs had recently decided against extending guarantees for syndicated ECB loans raised by corporates through the apex bank (RBI)'s automatic clearance window. The Finance Ministry had eased ECB norms last year, permitting schemes up to $3 million to tap international markets directly through the RBI.
